WHAT WAS AUTHORED: a configuration-only ROS 1 RosDriver for the RRBot two-joint arm. Primary control is two x-cap publications of std_msgs/Float64 position commands: /rrbot/joint1_position_controller/command is shown with its type by the rqt publisher at rrbot_control/launch/rrbot_rqt.perspective:63, and /rrbot/joint2_position_controller/command is shown with its type by README.md:28. Both controllers are effort_controllers/JointPositionController for the continuous joints joint1 and joint2 (rrbot_control/config/rrbot_control.yaml:7-15; rrbot_description/urdf/rrbot.xacro:55-61,90-96,199-219). The controller_manager spawner is launched under /rrbot (rrbot_control/launch/rrbot_control.launch:3-10), and the README quick start runs that launch file. The clone states no joint travel bound: both joints are continuous and the YAML gives PID gains only, so each input uses Limit.operator_required and site-limits.example.json carries explicitly example-only operator envelopes. The card's preferred upstream-simulator path is the Gazebo world plus ros_control; the offline gate has no ROS/Gazebo runtime and the clone ships no test harness, so the fake is a ROS-free RecordingRosTransport at F0 that records the advertise and publish operations on the two command topics; it runs no Gazebo, gazebo_ros_control, controller_manager, PID, physics, ROS graph or wall-clock loop, and every command record is a placeholder, not device state or a trajectory.

NOT COVERED: the clone names /rrbot/joint_states, /rrbot/laser/scan and /rrbot/camera1/image_raw but does not declare their ROS message types, and the helper requires an explicit type binding for every endpoint. I did not guess sensor_msgs/JointState, sensor_msgs/LaserScan or sensor_msgs/Image; those observations, the camera image path, the laser scan path, TF, /clock, RViz, the Gazebo world and controller_manager services are NOT COVERED. The camera is not presented as a completed integration. The rqt publisher's type is std_msgs/Float64 and the RViz display classes are not ROS message types.

WHY THE STOP IS MISSING: both control endpoints are fire-and-forget std_msgs/Float64 publications. The clone declares no runtime stop, pause, controller switch or reset service/action; the only stop-like option is the launch-time paused argument in rrbot_gazebo/launch/rrbot_world.launch:3-18, which is forwarded to gazebo_ros and is not a runtime endpoint. The Gazebo ROS API plugin is named at gazebo_tutorials/src/simple_world_plugin.cpp:12-16, but the clone does not name its pause/reset services. A zero-position publication is transmission only, so I did not declare it as a safe-state action or an e-stop. This is a genuine upstream stop gap, not a missing fake feature.

G8 TCAP-003 is an additional consequence of the same publication-only interface: the bridge's publication receipt is the fixed {published: true, confirmed: false} document, so two distinct position inputs have identical outputs, and the clone declares no readable state topic whose type the helper can bind. I did not add a fake-only read or an input-dependent receipt to hide that limitation. SAFE-028 follows from the missing stop. G1-G5 and G7 pass, so the declaration, citations, limits, reference and recorded wire traffic are checked; they do not prove a live ROS graph, controller behavior or physical stopping.
